question: In covering a distance of 162 km, Abhay takes 6 hours more than Sameer. If Abhay doubles his speed, then he would take 3 hours less than Sameer. Abhay's initial speed is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total time difference = 6 hours (more) + 3 hours (less) = 9 hours.

When **speed** is doubled (1 → 2), **time** taken becomes half (2 → 1).

Ratio of **Abhay's time**: 2 : 1. Difference = 1 unit.

1 unit = 9 hours ⇒ Original time (2 units) = 18 hours.

Abhay's initial speed = 162 km ÷ 18 hours = 9 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5b0c458a1b1f252011cbfc5188b12044b5384a5c0c7f95715df3a11717fd9e79.png] 

**Given:** Distance = 162 km, Time₁ = TimeSₐₘₑₑᵣ + 6, Time₂ = TimeSₐₘₑₑᵣ − 3.

**Formula Used:** Speed = Distance ÷ Time

⇒ Let **Abhay's initial speed** be x km/hr.

⇒ Time₁ − Time₂ = 9 hours

⇒ (162 ÷ x) − (162 ÷ 2x) = 9

⇒ (324 − 162) ÷ 2x = 9

⇒ 162 ÷ 2x = 9

⇒ 81 ÷ x = 9

⇒ x = 9 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 9 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Speed-Time Relationship

When distance is constant, **Speed** is inversely proportional to **Time** (S₁/S₂ = T₂/T₁).

Average Speed

For two equal distances with speeds x and y, **Average Speed** = 2xy ÷ (x + y).

Relative Speed

In the **same direction**, subtract speeds (u − v). In the **opposite direction**, add speeds (u + v).</p
